title: Adaptive-threshold degradation caused KEDA/HPA oscillation during bursty traffic — postmortem and action plan
creator: Ava Patel
description: During a customer-facing capacity event on 2026-03-01 we observed repeated under- and over-provisioning of serving pods for the text-generation tier. The immediate symptom was elevated latency and occasional 429s for short bursts of traffic from a few high-volume tenants. This ticket collects the timeline, root cause analysis, mitigation steps taken during the incident, and a prioritized action plan to prevent recurrence.
impact: ~4 hours of degraded latency for 3% of requests (p50 latency +120ms, p95 +1.1s) with transient 429s affecting two paying customers. No data exfiltration or correctness regressions.
timeline: 2026-03-01 09:02 UTC — Alert: increased 95th percentile latency for text-generation route triggered (SLO: 200ms).
2026-03-01 09:05 UTC — Spike in incoming QPS from two tenant IP ranges; KEDA reported scale-to-zero prevention firing but HPA replica count remained flat.
2026-03-01 09:08 UTC — First customer 429 observed; on-call routed traffic to fallback model variant to reduce latency.
2026-03-01 09:20 UTC — Incident declared; engineering on-call, runtime, and infra joined. Initial mitigation: temporarily increase HPA maxReplicas and enable explicit warm pool.
2026-03-01 09:40 UTC — Latency improved to near-normal; traffic patterns showed repeated short (10–40s) spikes that triggered KEDA but metric smoothing delayed HPA reaction, causing oscillation.

2026-03-01 11:30 UTC — Full mitigation: apply conservative debounce to KEDA trigger, enable prefix KV cache warmup for affected model family. Monitoring continued for 2 hours before declaring recovery.
detection: Automated SLO alerting for p95 latency on text-generation route plus customer reports. Root cause surfaced via correlated KEDA trigger logs, HPA metrics, and increased schedule churn in controller metrics.
root_cause: A recent change to adaptive threshold smoothing (merged in runtime-1.22) increased the metric aggregation window for KEDA-triggered scalers from 6s to 30s under low-sample scenarios. Bursty tenant traffic with short bursts (10–40s) produced high instantaneous load that KEDA registered, but the smoothed metric fed to HPA did not cross scale-up thresholds in time. In combination with an aggressive scale-down policy (30s cooldown) and no warm-pool prewarmed replicas, the system oscillated between insufficient capacity and reactive over-scaling once smoothing window ended. The net effect was oscillation and transient 429s/latency spikes.
mitigation_during_incident: 1) Temporarily reverted smoothing window to 8s for the affected KEDA scalers; 2) Increased HPA maxReplicas for text-generation to allow headroom; 3) Enabled model-family warm-pool with 2 prewarmed replicas; 4) Activated fallback routing to lower-cost model variant for affected tenants to keep latency within SLO.
long_term_analysis: The adaptive threshold feature improved noise resilience for steady-state traffic but failed under short-burst patterns. We found insufficient e2e tests that mimic multi-tenant burst profiles. The hybrid control loop between KEDA and HPA lacks explicit handoff semantics (no notion of 'burst window' vs 'sustained window'). Additionally, scaling cooldowns and warm pool orchestration were not coordinated across runtime and autoscaler configs.
action_items: ENG-302502: Implement burst-aware metric path — add a short-window (4-10s) fast-path metric feed for KEDA that bypasses long-term smoothing. Owner: Priya Rao. Due: 2026-03-17.

ENG-302503: Add e2e autoscaling test harness that simulates tenant burst patterns (10–60s) with multi-tenant interleaving; include assertions for no >1% 429s and p95 latency under configured SLO. Owner: Diego Martinez. Due: 2026-03-22.
ENG-302504: Introduce coordinated cooldown policy between KEDA and HPA with explicit handoff states (e.g., KEDA-burst, HPA-sustained). Owner: Marco Liu. Due: 2026-03-29.
ENG-302505: Provision warm-pool orchestration primitives in the autoscaling operator (configurable min-warm replicas per model-family). Owner: Sophia Nguyen. Due: 2026-04-05.
ENG-302506: Revisit default smoothing window and make it adaptive per traffic skew metric (document defaults and expose in console). Owner: Runtime team. Due: 2026-03-24.
ENG-302507: Create a runbook for on-call to quickly enable fallback routing and warm pools; include dashboard links and checklists. Owner: On-call SRE (rotation). Due: 2026-03-12.
ENG-302508: Customer communication: Send incident summary and mitigation steps to affected customers with credits offer. Owner: Customer Success (liaison: Maya Chen). Due: 2026-03-11.
ENG-302509: Post-deploy verification job — run 30-min burst simulation in staging after any autoscaler config change; block rollout on >0.5% 429 or p95 regression. Owner: CI Infra. Due: 2026-03-20.
followups: Design review for console UI to surface per-model-family autoscaling profiles and fast-path toggles. (PM + DX required)
Quantify cost impact of keeping warm-pool replicas for peak windows vs customer SLA penalties; include in Optimize recommendations.
Evaluate if canary rollout of smoothing changes should include synthetic burst tests before global rollout.
Security review not required for this change (no new data flows), but change audit logs will be enabled for autoscaler config edits.
notes: During the incident we observed increased controller CPU due to frequent evaluateScale calls; optimizing evaluateScale batching was deprioritized for this sprint but added to backlog.
Runtime-1.22 release note incorrectly advertised 'more conservative smoothing' without highlighting burst trade-offs; update release notes and docs.
Fallback routing proved effective and will be expanded to programmable tenant-level policies.
review_feedback: PM review (Riley Carter): request to prioritize runbook and customer comms — marked urgent and assigned to Customer Success.
Design review (Elena Park): suggest adding visual indicators for active warm pool and burst fast-path in the Console. Added as followup.
Security review (Omar Haddad): no issues but asked to ensure KMS keys for warm-pool control plane are audited.
final_summary: Root cause: smoothing window increased for low-sample KEDA metrics combined with aggressive scale-downs and missing warm-pool prewarmed replicas. Short-term mitigations restored SLOs. Long-term actions are prioritized to add a burst fast-path, improve e2e tests, coordinate cooldowns, and provide warm-pool orchestration. Customer communication completed and follow-ups scheduled.
